title: Detachment time calculation
description: Essential Criteria: The response must correctly calculate the time for the ball to detach from the rod as 0.1 s, using the vertical acceleration and rod length.

title: External force work
description: Essential Criteria: The response must correctly calculate the work done by the horizontal external force F as 2 × 10⁻⁵ J, using the work-energy theorem.

title: Velocity range for impact
description: Essential Criteria: The response must correctly determine the range of rod velocities for the ball to hit the left side of the baffle as 1 m/s < v₀ < 2 m/s.

title: Lorentz force analysis
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly identify the Lorentz force as the source of the ball's vertical acceleration and relate it to the rod's horizontal velocity.

title: Kinematic modeling
description: Important Criteria: The solution must apply kinematic equations for uniformly accelerated motion to describe the ball's vertical motion along the rod.

title: Post-detachment motion analysis
description: Important Criteria: For part (3), the solution must analyze the ball's subsequent circular motion in the magnetic field and its geometric intersection with the baffle.

title: Energy theorem application
description: Optional Criteria: The solution may explicitly use the work-energy theorem to connect the external work to the change in the ball's kinetic energy.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the direction of the Lorentz force (or the sign of the charge's influence) is incorrectly determined, affecting acceleration or trajectory.

title: Unit inconsistency
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if calculations fail to use consistent SI units (meters, seconds, Teslas, Coulombs) leading to incorrect numerical results.
